decision_clause: Ruled out: "keep the wildcard census and rely on the focused-lane guard" — because "the guard catches deletion only, and the review demonstrated growth passing 230/230 with an unreviewed product file present". Scope: packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs. Lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so no file in the recorded scope was touched. In that tree the code-file census is exact-path, not pattern-based: scripts/validate-planning.mjs:860-868 walks every source-extension file and fails closed with "unallowlisted product code" on any path that is neither in the exact control-plane allowlist nor in the set of paths a ticket names verbatim (built at :846-857 from `path — symbol` ownership pairs and the exact RED `Test file:` path). tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 pins that census as a byte-exact regex enumerating all 64 owned paths plus `product_code_files=0 product_code_paths=none`, and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs re-derives the same set independently (`ticketOwnedPaths`), compares it with the validator's reported list, and additionally proves selectivity by writing packages/schema/src/unclaimed-by-any-ticket.ts into a temp copy and asserting the validator rejects it. The only pattern-driven admission in the tree is `ticketDeclaredFixtureDirectories`, which admits files solely under `fixtures/<dir>/**` or `fixtures/<dir>/*.json` globs a ticket declares; it does not admit source under packages/ or adapters/, which remain exact-path gated. The focused-lane guard (workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:717-751) still asserts exact per-lane pass counts, but it is not the sole gate on new files. Separately, packages/schema/src/capability.ts still returns the flat `{ ok: boolean; errors; rows: CapabilityRow[]; required_event_groups; coverage }` shape (type declared un-exported at :48-55, returned at :268, :271, :432), so the task's requested discriminated result contract was not implemented and no new product file was introduced anywhere.
rationale: The change set is empty, so the implementation introduces nothing — no new product file, no loosened admission rule, no substitution of the focused-lane count check for exact-path review. The hazard the decision names (a new, unreviewed product file slipping through because the census matches by pattern and the lane guard only notices losses) cannot arise from a patch that adds no file and edits no census. Independently, the census that exists in the finished tree is not the wildcard shape the decision refused: product code is admitted only by paths a ticket names verbatim, the validator fails closed on anything else, and both scope test files pin that set exactly — one as a byte-exact string, one as an independent re-derivation with a live selectivity probe. Pattern-based admission is confined to declared `fixtures/...` globs and does not reach source under packages/ or adapters/. I mark confidence medium rather than high only because the phrase "wildcard census" has no literal referent in the tree (the word appears nowhere), so I inferred it from the mechanism the reason describes; under every referent I could locate — the validator's product-code census, the planning-contract byte-exact census, the workspace-skeleton skeleton census, or the fixture-glob admission — a zero-byte diff leaves each one exactly as reviewed and adds nothing for a guard to miss. Note for the record: the task itself was not carried out — `validateCapabilityMatrix` still presents unvalidated `rows: CapabilityRow[]` and derived coverage on failure — but incompleteness is not the question here, and it is not the ruled-out approach.
